photos.c: FRONT COVER (Photo:R.Linstead) Jim Vivian (64) wins the All-England Schools sprint title in 10.1 from his Surrey County team-mate and training companion Tony Oke (10.1). In August, Vivian went on to clock 9.9 in the AAA's Junior Champs; Nash of South Africa being the only man to beat him.
THE A.A.A. 4 X 110 YARDS JUNIOR RELAY CHAMPIONS 1965 Left to right: J. Vivian, D. Gleeson, C. Martin, J. Mitchell.
Belgrave Harriers 4X220 Relay Team. l.to r. J.Vivian, C.Martin,R.Nelson,J.Mitchell.
THE SURREY CHAMPIONSHIP FINALS. TOP: Jim Vivian splits A. Tymms (Surrey AC) and R. Woodland (Hercules) to finish 2nd in the 220 yds with 22.0 seconds.
Barrie Kelly (Lancs) gets a flyer on JIM VIVIAN (Surrey/BELS) at the start of the 100yds semi-final in the Inter-Counties. JIM was eliminated, controversially, after a blanket finish for third.
Tymms wins the 100 from VIVIAN with MARTIN fifth
FRONT COVER: (Photo by Ed Lacey) Jim Vivian (38) matches world-record holder Paul Nash stride for stride in his heat of the A.A.A. 100 yds at White City. Both qualified in 10.1.
JIM VIVIAN streaks to a 100 metres win in the 'Brockman' Trophy.

Just back from injury, JIM VIVIAN splits Knowles (Brighton & H.) and Reynolds (TVH) in the Brockman 100. But he was unable to recover his old dash in time for the A.A.A. Championships where he was eliminated in 11.2.

Left: Flashback! Twentynine years ago at Crystal Palace, and Jim Vivian, Chris Martin, Robert Nelson and Dave Mitchell pose for the camera of Ed. Lacey after placing 6th in the final of the A.A.A. 4 x 220yds relay Championship in 1:31.9.

photo.caption: FRONT COVER (Photo:R.Linstead) Jim Vivian (64) wins the All-England Schools sprint title in 10.1 from his Surrey County team-mate and training companion Tony Oke (10.1). In August, Vivian went on to clock 9.9 in the AAA's Junior Champs; Nash of South Africa being the only man to beat him.
